tldr: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 and the unguarded Mythos 5 model on Jun 9; the first day-one hands-on called it "something of a beast" — powerful but slow and expensive — as launch coverage flagged controversial usage terms. Two days in, a sustained read called Fable 5 "relentlessly proactive." Then on Jun 12-13 the story turned: a US export-control directive, citing national security, suspended access, and coverage recast the launch as too dangerous to release. A Jun 15 recap framed it as temporary. By Jun 20 access is back on Amazon Bedrock — but only via provider_data_share, sending prompts and outputs to Anthropic for 30-day retention with human review.
whats_new: Access is partially restored: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are usable on Amazon Bedrock again, but require opting into provider_data_share — prompts and outputs go to Anthropic for 30-day retention with human review, a break from how previous Bedrock models kept inference data private.
why_it_matters: A flagship can swing from GA launch to government-ordered suspension and back to a conditional, data-sharing-only return within days. The Bedrock terms make the catch concrete: regaining access can mean surrendering prompt/output confidentiality, which matters for anything handling sensitive data.

status.detail: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 launched "made safe for general use," were pulled by a US export-control directive, then returned on Amazon Bedrock — but only with provider_data_share, sending prompts and outputs to Anthropic for 30-day retention with human review.

beats.headline: Claude Fable 5 + Mythos 5 ship — a "beast" with controversial terms
beats.summary: Anthropic ships the Mythos-class models on Jun 9; the first day-one hands-on, without early access, calls Fable 5 something of a beast — powerful but slow and expensive — and launch coverage flags controversial usage terms.

beats.headline: A powerful but "relentlessly proactive" beast
beats.summary: After two days, the first sustained hands-on reads Fable 5 as relentlessly proactive, deploying every trick to reach a goal.

beats.headline: US export-control directive suspends access
beats.summary: On national-security grounds the US government orders access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 suspended; coverage reframes the launch as "too dangerous to release."

beats.headline: Reframed as a temporary suspension — no re-enable date
beats.summary: An outside recap ties the takedown to the export-control directive and frames it as temporary rather than permanent.

beats.headline: Back on Bedrock — but only with data-sharing opted in
beats.summary: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 return on Amazon Bedrock, gated behind provider_data_share: prompts and outputs go to Anthropic for 30-day retention with human review.

open_questions: Is the Bedrock data-sharing requirement temporary, or the permanent condition of access?
Is Fable 5 / Mythos 5 returning anywhere outside Bedrock, on standard private-inference terms?
Does the export-control directive still apply, or has it been lifted for the Bedrock path?
How is the 30-day retention with human review reconciled with enterprise data-governance commitments?
take_for_builders: If you re-enable Fable 5 / Mythos 5 on Bedrock, read the provider_data_share terms first: access now means prompts and outputs are retained by Anthropic for 30 days with human review. Keep a fallback model wired in rather than hard-coding a single flagship tier.
